query_text: Why do we turn pale/green when we're sick?

messages.content: Why do we turn pale/green when we're sick?

message.content:
When you’re sick, your body often **reduces blood flow to the skin** and redirects it toward vital organs, which can make you look **pale**.[1][3] Illness can also cause **dehydration, fever, shock, or anemia**, all of which can reduce the blood or oxygen reaching the skin and make pallor more noticeable.[1][2][3]

The **greenish** look people sometimes mention usually isn’t true green skin; it’s more often a mix of **paleness, a tired/ashen appearance, and sometimes nausea** making the face look unhealthy.[2][4] Research on “sickness cues” found that **pale skin** is one of the strongest visual signs people associate with being sick.[4]

If someone is suddenly very pale, has trouble breathing, feels faint, or looks pale along with blue lips or chest pain, that can signal a more serious problem and needs urgent medical attention.[1][3]
